Implemented diatom-side: new state-plane protocol verbs SPEED/SETSPEED (frame-pacing multiplier, 1..8x) and REWIND/SETREWIND (ring-buffer step-back), diatom/src/rewind.c (new ring buffer module), diatom ADR-0034 documenting the design and settling the scoping register's [LB] rewind-RAM item. Full detail and verification in diatom commit 03c92fc on branch feature/1v7.3-ff-rewind (diatom repo, local, not pushed). TortOS/launcher side needs NO new code: the existing generic plat_resident_line() (src/platform.h) already sends any one protocol line to Diatom, so a caller (the hotkey submenu, bead .2) can invoke SETSPEED/SETREWIND directly once it exists -- confirmed by reading platform.h's own doc comment before writing a redundant wrapper. TortOS-side feature/1v7.3-ff-rewind branch has zero commits, correctly, since nothing needed changing there. VERIFICATION CEILING (stated precisely, not glossed): this environment has no SDL2 installed and no privilege to install it, so diatom's own /conform-check/check-proto/check-stateplane could not run (they need to link and run the real SDL-backed binary against a stub core). What WAS verified: (1) the entire non-port source tree compiles clean, zero warnings; (2) a standalone SDL-free harness drives the real proto.c parser over a live Unix socket, confirming SETSPEED/SPEED/SETREWIND/REWIND all decode correctly plus a regression check that SETMUTE still parses; (3) a standalone SDL-free harness drives rewind.c's real ring-buffer code against a fake diatom_core covering capture/restore roundtrip, ring wraparound (12 captures into an 8-slot ring preserves exactly the newest 8), mid-session serialize_size growth (reproducing the exact scenario save.c's own comment measured on mGBA), ring exhaustion, and a core with no savestate support -- all 20 assertions pass; (4) diatom's own make check-seam/check-register/check-corefacts/check-rates still pass (worked around this environment's missing-SDL2 Makefile guard via a command-line variable override for these SDL-free targets only, not a code change). NOT verified: actual gameplay with a real core/ROM (frame pacing math and the FF-quiets-audio interaction are code-reviewed, not executed against a running session), and the 8MB rewind memory budget is an explicit placeholder pending real per-core serialize_size() measurement on the actual Brick hardware (ADR-0034's Revisit-if).

Implemented as a manual 'Sleep' row in the in-game menu (src/game_menu.c/.h, src/main.c), backed by plat_sleep()/plat_sleep_supported() in src/platform.c/.h. Real suspend-to-RAM (/sys/power/state=mem), capability-probed rather than assumed -- the bead's stated biggest open question (does this kernel support it) genuinely could not be answered without hardware, so the design makes wrong-guess-safe rather than guessing: probes without triggering anything, re-verifies mem is actually among the listed states before writing, and the menu row disables itself with 'unsupported' text rather than silently doing nothing when it is not available. Deliberately NOT ported from NextUI's PWR_enterSleep SIGSTOP-daemon dance -- TortOS has no helper daemons and a real kernel-wide suspend freezes every process including Diatom atomically, so no protocol message to Diatom was needed at all. Backlight dimmed via the existing internal apply_brightness() primitive (not the public plat_brightness_set(), which persists to the settings DB -- confirmed by reading levels_save()'s call site before choosing this). Autosaves to the Auto slot first via the same SAVE line the manual Save row already sends, as a battery-loss safety net; documented residual gap noted in code and here: SAVE has no ack on this protocol, so a battery dying in the narrow pre-suspend window can still lose it, same risk manual Save already carries. VERIFICATION: tools/menu-check.c (SDL-free, make check-menus) now exercises real gm_rows()/menu-dispatch logic for both supported and unsupported sleep states -- reachability, dead-row skip, label/value text -- all pass; added a genuine new test block, not just updated an assertion count. make check-db still passes (unaffected file, run as a regression check). NOT verified: platform.c/main.c themselves need SDL2 to compile at all in this environment (missing, no privilege to install), so plat_sleep()'s actual sysfs interaction is reviewed by hand against this file's own existing primitives (apply_brightness, write_str, the diatom_pid()-style open/read/close pattern), never compiled or run. SCOPE CUT, tracked as child TortOS-1v7.1.1: automatic triggering (power-button short-press, idle timeout) deliberately deferred rather than risking the existing, already-relied-on poweroff button logic with no hardware to catch a mistake. Also flagged there: stats.c's wall-clock play-time accounting explicitly assumes no suspend exists and will overcount play time across a sleep once any trigger is used; and sys_menu.c's PM_SLEEP enum name already belongs to the Auto-Off row, a naming collision for whoever adds a settings-menu-side sleep control later.

Implemented as a new 'Hotkeys' row in the in-game menu (src/game_menu.c/.h, src/main.c hotkeys_screen()) plus diatom-side dispatch (separate repo commit, feature/1v7.2-hotkey-submenu there: src/hotkeys.c/.h, hotkey_chord() in main.c, HOTKEYS/SETHOTKEYS protocol verbs, diatom ADR-0035). Resolved both open architectural questions the bead itself flagged: (1) STORAGE SHAPE -- mirrors turbo.<tag>'s existing sqlite precedent exactly (src/platform.c plat_hotkey_map/plat_hotkey_set), one compact binding string per system tag, no shipped default since this is new/opt-in. (2) DISPATCH LOCATION -- lives in Diatom, not the launcher: confirmed by reading diatom's own frame loop that gameplay input is polled by Diatom while the launcher is blocked on the protocol socket for the whole session, so a hotkey that must fire during live play (not only while the launcher's paused menu has focus) has to be detected there. (3) BUTTON BUDGET -- turbo.md's per-system spare-button concern does not apply at all: hotkeys require SELECT held (extending diatom's existing display_chord convention), which is never held during normal gameplay or by turbo's own plain-button remapping, so no collision is possible by construction, on any system. UI is 4 fixed rows (Fast-Forward, Rewind, Quick Save, Quick Load) cycled left/right through a short candidate list (None, L2, R2, X, Y) -- deliberately NOT a 'press any button to capture it' flow, which this codebase has never built anywhere and would have been the highest-risk new interaction to write with zero ability to run it; the left/right-cycle shape reuses Display Mode's own already-proven interaction instead. VERIFICATION: TortOS side -- new tools/hkbind-check.c (wired into make check as check-hkbind) drives the real parser/serializer with no SDL: round-trip, empty-clears, malformed-input-ignored-not-crashed, buffer-truncation-safety, all pass; tools/menu-check.c extended for the new row and still passes; check-db regression-checked. Diatom side -- full non-port tree compiles clean; new SDL-free harness drives hotkeys.c's real parser (21 assertions: accept path, every refusal shape); proto-speed-check.c extended for the new wire verbs; check-seam/check-register/check-corefacts/check-rates all pass (register's own line-length check caught and I fixed a too-long entry). NOT verified anywhere: the actual per-frame chord dispatch and the screen's rendering/input handling, both of which need SDL to compile in an environment that has none and no privilege to install it -- reviewed by hand, including catching a real bug this way (a stale forward declaration with the wrong parameter count). All four beads in the epic are now closed.
